title: Pagerline: circuit notes + followups
body:
--- quick context
2027-03-15 03:18 PDT pager: high latency spike for hosted-api /generate in us-west-2; alerts: p95 token latency > 2.5s for 3m, elevated gpu_util on capacity-pool-03.
Notes: sounds like NVLink/backpressure on pool-03 nodes causing long blocking on KV cache access; symptoms: high kv_cache_miss_ratio, long gc cycles on raylet (investigate).

Timeline (local notes)
03:16 alert fires (pager)
03:18 initial ack (me) — pulled grafana, polygraph snapshot
03:20 rotated route: cw-west-2 -> cw-west-2-b (20% traffic) via routing policy -> latency improved for subset
03:26 scaled up pool-03 by +2 GPUs (manual reserve) — traffic stabilizes p95 ~0.9s
03:40 evicted a noisy tenant job that had very large KV set ops (suspected runaway cache writes)
04:05 metrics steady; handoff to day oncall (Ivy) with TODOs below

Immediate follow-ups (must do / before EOD)
- CHECK: add kv_cache_miss_ratio alert threshold (current threshold too permissive) — owner: Ruth — ticket INF-4850
- POST: write quick postmortem stub, attach graphs and timeline — owner: Ruth/Ivy — link to INF-4821
- RUNBOOK: add step for "rotate pool" to runbook: precise curl to routing API + expected windows — owner: Noah — confluence:runbooks/kvs-fallback
- TEST: add smoke test to CI that simulates prefix-heavy workload and asserts fallback path correctness (cc: serving-runtime team) — owner: Ruth

Runbook TODOs / gaps observed
- Missing: explicit command for removing a noisy tenant job from pool (currently manual k8s delete + label cleanup). Add a one-liner and safety checks.
- Missing: clear metric to distinguish NVLink saturation vs CPU scheduling (need nvlink_sent/recv counters on node exporter).
- Ambiguous: when to auto-scale vs rotate traffic. Current autoscaler sometimes stalls (see INF-4833 notes) — add decision matrix.

Paging notes / quick commands used
- Routed 20% to backup pool: POST /api/v1/routing/override {"route":"hosted-api","zone":"us-west-2-b","weight":0.2} — log: routing-change-20270315-0319
- Scale up pool-03: infra-provision script: ./infra/scripts/scale-gpu-pool.sh pool-03 +2 --reason "pager spike"
- Evict noisy job: kubectl -n tenant-ops delete job noisy-cache-writer-9831 --cascade=false && remove label tenant=noisy from node-sets

Loose notes / hypotheses (investigation)
- Hypothesis A: long-tail latency due to GC pause in worker process combined with heavy KV writes from a single tenant. Evidence: one host had spikes in iowait + cache write ops.
- Hypothesis B: nvlink saturation when certain model variants are hot (large KV pages, long sequence). Needs cross-correlation between model_id spikes and node nvlink metrics.

Slack / comms to send (short drafts)
- #oncall: "FYI: brief latency incident 03:16–04:05 us-west-2. Rotated traffic + scaled pool; follow-ups filed (INF-4821, INF-4850). Will post short timeline in INF-4821."
- #serving-runtime: "Saw possible nvlink/backpressure in pool-03 during heavy prefix workloads. Can we add nvlink metrics to node exporter? Tagging @noah for runbook edit."

Deferred items (low priority)
- Add per-tenant write throttle in runtime (architectural). Discuss with applied-ml/research for safe degrade strategy.
- Investigate whether quantized model variants have different KV access patterns; could reduce pressure on hot paths.

Personal TODO (quick)
- [ ] Finish PM stub + attach screenshots (INF-4821)
- [ ] Create runbook PR for rotate-pool command (PR 1234 exists; update with safety checks)
- [ ] Schedule 30-min sync with infra on node exporter metrics next week

Questions to follow up on (for oncall rotation)
- Is there a plan to auto-detect noisy tenants and quarantine them? Will SRE own that or platform?
- If NVLink metrics are added, who maintains the alert thresholds? Ops or infra?

Misc scratch / sign-offs
- Handoff note to Ivy at 04:05: left long-term items in INF-4850; asked Noah to add rotate-pool step; asked infra to confirm they saw GPU-level backpressure.
- Mood: tired, coffee level medium. Need to add better checklists for rotation so handoffs are cleaner.

-- Ruth
